description:
Hi! 

I’m a B.Tech Electrical & Electronics Engineering student passionate about space Exploration.

For the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, I'm building a visual story about all the old NASA rovers, landers, and probes left behind on the Moon and Mars, and the amazing science they found. I'm building it for school kids so they can get excited about space too. I'm working solo right now and trying to use real NASA data to make it look clean and actually fun to read.
summary: Silent Sentinels (Diary of the Forgotten Machines) is an interactive digital storybook and visual field guide designed to introduce school-age space enthusiasts (ages 10–15) to NASA’s historic hardware resting across the Moon, Mars, and deep space.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Silent Sentinels (Diary of the Forgotten Machines) is an interactive digital storybook and visual field guide built for school-age space enthusiasts (ages 10–15). Students begin by choosing a destination—the Moon, Mars, or Deep Space—and selecting a historic NASA spacecraft or rover. Each chapter presents a 60-second first-person diary entry written from the machine’s perspective, paired with an "Under the Hood" engineering card explaining its power systems, instruments, why its mission ended, and real orbital photos showing where it rests today. A short 2-question "Space Historian" mini-quiz at the end of each entry reinforces key scientific takeaways.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Most young learners only hear about active missions like Perseverance and Artemis, while pioneering hardware like the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Opportunity, InSight, and Voyager 1 remains tucked away in dense technical archives. By turning silent off-world artifacts into relatable storytellers, Silent Sentinels bridges the gap between complex planetary science and middle-school comprehension—sparking early STEM curiosity and showing students how past engineering breakthroughs made today's missions possible.

Tools & Software Used

Presentation & Visual Design: Google Slides and PDF export tools for layout, visual cards, and typography.

Research & Scientific Verification: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC), Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (HiRISE), and the NASA Science / NSSDC Master Catalog for authentic mission specifications and orbital imagery.

AI Assistance: Google Gemini for structuring narrative outlines, refining kid-friendly storytelling phrasing, and organizing project documentation.

Creativity & Key Considerations

Rather than listing dry dates and technical specs, the project uses first-person personification—allowing retired rovers and landers to share their own "memories" in clear, age-appropriate language. During development, we prioritized scientific accuracy (ensuring every engineering detail and discovery matches verified NASA mission logs), visual clarity for young readers, and accessible web-based sharing so any student or teacher can view the guide effortlessly.
